gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: The cafe ___ we first met has closed down.
gaps.hint: location: we met in the cafe
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' for places; 'which' would need a preposition ('in which').

gaps.sentence: That's the office ___ I worked for ten years.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which'; 'I worked the office' shows the place role of the gap.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The person to ___ I addressed the letter has moved house.
gaps.hint: after a preposition, the object form for people
gaps.explanation: After a preposition the object pronoun 'whom' is required for people; 'that' and 'who' cannot follow a preposition.

gaps.sentence: This is the beach ___ we used to play as children.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces place information; 'we used to play' already has a subject and object, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: There are times ___ I really miss my home town.
gaps.explanation: 'There are times when ...' is a standard pattern; 'when' stands for 'at which'.
